cancer_indication: Hormone receptor (HR)–positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women (adjuvant therapy after 2–3 years of tamoxifen and for advanced/metastatic ER+ breast cancer after tamoxifen); with ovarian suppression (OFS) in premenopausal HR+ disease (SOFT/TEXT trials).
moa: Exemestane is a steroidal, irreversible (“suicide”) aromatase inhibitor that permanently inactivates CYP19A1 (aromatase), blocking conversion of androgens to estrogens and sharply reducing estrogen levels. Estrogen deprivation suppresses estrogen receptor–mediated transcription, leading to G1 arrest and apoptosis in ER+ breast tumor cells. In premenopausal women, exemestane requires concurrent ovarian suppression to be effective. Resistance can arise via upregulation of alternate growth pathways (e.g., HER/EGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR) or ESR1 mutations, whereas high ER expression and intact hormone signaling sensitize tumors to exemestane.

REACTOME_ESTROGEN_BIOSYNTHESIS.description: Covers enzymatic conversion of androgens to estrogens, including the aromatase (CYP19A1) step producing estrone/estradiol.
REACTOME_ESTROGEN_BIOSYNTHESIS.interpretation:
Provides the estrogen ligand supply that supports growth and transcriptional programs in ER+ breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- ER+ breast tumors selected for Exemestane typically show active peripheral/intratumoral estrogen biosynthesis via aromatase (CYP19A1). High estrogen production makes the tumor dependent on this axis; irreversible aromatase blockade by Exemestane depletes estrogen and suppresses growth.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Upregulated aromatase/estrogen biosynthesis in ER+ luminal breast cancer indicates strong dependence on CYP19A1-derived estrogen, so irreversible aromatase inhibition by exemestane produces marked ER pathway shutdown and clinical benefit.
DrugBank:DB00990; ChEMBL:CHEMBL1200374; Reactome:R-HSA-193144; FDA label:020753
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with high estrogen biosynthesis also harbor dominant HER2/PI3K signaling or ESR1 mutations, making growth only partially aromatase-dependent and reducing AI benefit despite an “up” biosynthesis signature.
Reactome:R-HSA-193144; KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Bulk profiling may show modest estrogen biosynthesis even when a tumor relies on low-level local aromatase activity, so further CYP19A1 blockade can still produce benefit in some ER+ breast cancers.
DrugBank:DB00990; Reactome:R-HSA-193144
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ER-low or endocrine-independent breast cancers often exhibit low estrogen biosynthesis pathway activity and are intrinsically resistant to aromatase inhibitors because there is little CYP19A1-driven estrogen to remove.
Reactome:R-HSA-193144; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Exemestane irreversibly inactivates CYP19A1, sharply downregulating estrogen biosynthesis and depriving ER+ tumor cells of ligand, which underlies clinical responses in postmenopausal HR+ breast cancer.
DrugBank:DB00990; ChEMBL:CHEMBL1200374; Reactome:R-HSA-193144
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In resistant clones, exemestane still suppresses estrogen biosynthesis but survival is maintained via HER2/EGFR or PI3K/mTOR escape pathways, so pathway downregulation alone does not ensure sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB00990; Reactome:R-HSA-193144; KEGG:hsa04012

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: An irreversible aromatase inhibitor cannot increase functional estrogen biosynthesis in sensitive tumors; any apparent “up” signature would reflect stromal contamination or assay noise rather than true pathway activation.
DrugBank:DB00990; Reactome:R-HSA-193144
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Chronic AI therapy may induce compensatory upregulation of steroidogenic enzymes or aromatase transcription, but CYP19A1 remains covalently inhibited so apparent biosynthesis “up” mainly reflects adaptive resistant clones using extra-aromatase estrogen sources.
DrugBank:DB00990; Reactome:R-HSA-193144; MSigDB:HALLMARK_STEROID_HORMONE_BIOSYNTHESIS

REACTOME_ESTROGEN_DEPENDENT_GENE_EXPRESS.description: Represents estrogen-dependent transcriptional activation driven by estrogen receptor signaling programs that regulate downstream gene expression.
REACTOME_ESTROGEN_DEPENDENT_GENE_EXPRESS.interpretation:
Sustains ER-driven proliferative gene programs in ER+ breast cancer that are central to endocrine dependence.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Classical AI-sensitive tumors rely on ligand-dependent ERα signaling: high ER expression and ER-regulated transcription drive proliferation. Depriving estrogen with Exemestane shuts down this ESR pathway. ESR1 activating mutations or loss of ER reduce AI benefit and drive resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High estrogen-dependent gene expression (ESR1 target programs) indicates strong ER signaling, so estrogen deprivation with exemestane efficiently downregulates these genes and halts proliferation in luminal tumors.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors with very high ER programs but concurrent HER2/PI3K activation or ESR1 ligand-independent mutations may maintain ER target transcription despite estrogen loss, resulting in AI resistance despite an “up” signature.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: After prior endocrine therapy, some partially ER-suppressed tumors remain modestly ER-driven and can still derive benefit from further estrogen depletion with exemestane.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low ESR1 target gene expression indicates ER-independence or ER loss, so blocking estrogen synthesis with exemestane has minimal impact on tumor growth.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective exemestane treatment collapses estrogen-dependent transcriptional programs, reflected as downregulation of ESR1 target gene sets and reduction in proliferation-related transcripts.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In some resistant tumors, ER programs are partially repressed by estrogen loss but growth is sustained via parallel HER2/EGFR or PI3K/mTOR pathways, so decreased ESR signaling does not translate to sensitivity.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: True estrogen-dependent gene expression should not increase in a biologically sensitive tumor when ligand supply is cut off by aromatase inhibition; any “up” ESR signature with response would be artifactual.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Acquired ESR1 activating mutations or growth factor cross-talk can reactivate ER target gene expression despite estrogen depletion, producing an “up” ESR signature and clinical resistance to AIs.
Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; MSigDB:STEIN_ESR1_TARGETS; PMID:24752075

WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.description: Broad estrogen signaling encompassing nuclear (“genomic”) and membrane-associated (“non-genomic”) estrogen receptor pathways.
WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.interpretation:
Key driver of ER-associated proliferation and differentiation programs in ER+ breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Broad estrogen signaling (genomic nuclear ER and rapid non-genomic membrane ER effects) is typically active in hormone-dependent tumors. Exemestane indirectly suppresses both arms by lowering estrogen levels; high baseline estrogen signaling therefore predicts benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Upregulated estrogen signaling networks (membrane and nuclear ER modules) in HR+ breast cancer reflect estrogen addiction, so blocking estrogen synthesis with exemestane effectively shuts down this pathway.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; DrugBank:DB00990; MSigDB:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors with high estrogen signaling also exhibit dominant HER2/IGF1R–PI3K signaling, allowing partial bypass of estrogen dependence and limiting AI efficacy.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; KEGG:hsa04012; KEGG:hsa04151

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Borderline ER+ tumors with modest estrogen signaling can still benefit from additional suppression of intracrine estrogens via exemestane, especially after tamoxifen.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; NCT00066573 (IES trial)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Tumors with low estrogen signaling (e.g., ER−/basal-like or heavily pretreated endocrine-refractory clones) are unlikely to respond because exemestane targets a largely inactive pathway.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Exemestane reduces estrogen levels to near-zero, leading to broad downregulation of estrogen signaling components across nuclear and membrane ER modules in responding HR+ disease.
DrugBank:DB00990; WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Estrogen signaling can still be transcriptionally dampened by exemestane even when cells survive via HER2/EGFR/PI3K escape, so pathway downregulation may coexist with resistance.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: In a truly sensitive tumor, estrogen signaling should not increase while aromatase is covalently inhibited; an “up” pathway score with response would not reflect genuine exemestane biology.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Chronic AI exposure plus ESR1 mutation or strong growth factor cross-talk may lead to apparent re-activation of estrogen signaling despite therapy, marking acquired resistance.
WikiPathways:WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING; MSigDB:STEIN_ESR1_TARGETS; PMID:24752075

REACTOME_METABOLISM_OF_STEROID_HORMONES.description: Steroid hormone metabolic network from cholesterol-derived intermediates through sex steroid production and interconversion.
REACTOME_METABOLISM_OF_STEROID_HORMONES.interpretation:
Shapes the steroid hormone environment that influences ER-driven tumor biology and endocrine responsiveness.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In postmenopausal HR+ breast cancer, steroid hormone metabolism is skewed toward local estrone/estradiol production from adrenal precursors. High activity of this estrogenic branch provides substrate for ER signaling and makes tumors more susceptible to aromatase inhibition with Exemestane.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Upregulated steroid hormone metabolism provides abundant androgen substrate for aromatase, reinforcing estrogen production and ER-driven growth that can be effectively blocked by exemestane.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; Reactome:R-HSA-193144; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Strong steroidogenic activity may also fuel alternative receptor pathways (e.g., progesterone or androgen receptor) or permit local estrogen production even after partial aromatase block, contributing to AI resistance in some tumors.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Breast cancers with modest steroidogenic signatures but intact ER can still rely on low-level circulating estrogens, such that additional aromatase inhibition remains beneficial.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Tumors with low steroid hormone metabolism are less dependent on intracrine estrogen synthesis and often behave endocrine-resistant, limiting exemestane’s impact.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Exemestane interrupts the androgen-to-estrogen branch of steroid metabolism, lowering downstream estrone/estradiol and contributing to tumor regression in ER+ disease.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; Reactome:R-HSA-193144; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even when exemestane suppresses estrogenic steroid metabolism, resistant clones may exploit other steroid pathways (e.g., androgenic signaling or glucocorticoid responses) to maintain growth.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: The specific estrogenic branch of steroid metabolism should not be functionally increased by a suicide aromatase inhibitor in sensitive tumors; any apparent “up” reflects measurement artifact.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Adaptive rewiring of steroidogenic enzymes (e.g., increased upstream androgen production) under AI pressure may produce an apparent global increase in steroid metabolism while tumors escape via non-ER pathways.
Reactome:R-HSA-196071; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Growth factor receptor signaling via ERBB family members (including EGFR/HER2) and downstream proliferative pathways (e.g., MAPK).
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation:
Can provide alternative proliferative/survival signaling that bypasses ER dependence in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Upregulated EGFR/HER2→MAPK signaling provides a ligand-independent growth/survival route that bypasses ER. In Exemestane-resistant models, Exemestane induces AREG, which stimulates EGFR–MAPK and sustains proliferation despite estrogen depletion; clinically, HER2/EGFR activation is a key endocrine-resistance mechanism.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderately upregulated HER2/EGFR signaling can coexist with strong ER dependence, so some HER2-low/ER+ tumors still respond well to aromatase inhibition with exemestane.
KEGG:hsa04012; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High ERBB2/EGFR pathway activation in ER+ breast cancer drives ligand-independent proliferation and is a well-described mechanism of endocrine and AI resistance.
KEGG:hsa04012; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986; PMID:18381432

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low ERBB signaling leaves ER as the dominant driver of growth, making tumors more dependent on estrogen and typically more responsive to exemestane.
KEGG:hsa04012; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ERBB-low tumors can still be resistant to AI due to downstream PI3K/mTOR activation or loss of ER, despite a “down” HER2/EGFR signature.
KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Estrogen deprivation can secondarily reduce expression of some ER-regulated growth factor ligands/receptors, leading to partial downregulation of ERBB signaling in responders.
KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ERBB signaling may transiently fall after estrogen depletion but rebound or be bypassed via other RTKs, so sustained resistance is maintained despite initial pathway downregulation.
KEGG:hsa04012; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In a highly inflamed or regressing tumor, increased infiltration of ERBB-expressing non-malignant cells could artifactually raise pathway signatures while the malignant ERBB-driven signaling remains controlled by endocrine therapy.
KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:REACTOME_ERBB2_SIGNALING
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In exemestane-resistant cells, amphiregulin/EGFR autocrine loops and HER2 activation upregulate MAPK signaling, allowing growth despite estrogen depletion.
KEGG:hsa04012; PMID:18381432; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core survival and growth signaling axis involving PI3K, AKT, and mTOR that regulates metabolism, protein synthesis, and proliferation.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation:
A major pro-survival/proliferation program frequently activated in breast cancer and linked to endocrine escape mechanisms.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Constitutive PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation (PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss, RTK activation) uncouples proliferation and survival from ER/estrogen, leading to intrinsic or acquired resistance to aromatase inhibitors. This underpins clinical benefit from combining endocrine therapy with mTOR (everolimus) or PI3K/AKT inhibitors in HR+ disease.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with PI3K pathway activation remain ER-addicted, so AIs like exemestane can still be effective, although combination with mTOR/PI3K inhibitors yields deeper responses.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; NCT00863655 (BOLERO-2)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Hyperactivated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling provides estrogen-independent survival and is a classic mechanism of resistance to aromatase inhibition in ER+ breast cancer.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; PMID:18381432

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling reflects reliance on ER-driven mitogenic cues, so depriving estrogen with exemestane is usually highly effective.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some ER-low tumors with low bulk PI3K signatures may still resist AIs via alternative pathways (e.g., cyclin E overexpression or EMT), despite a “down” PI3K/AKT score.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Exemestane does not directly target PI3K, but in AI-sensitive tumors, upstream ER withdrawal can secondarily reduce PI3K/mTOR activity accompanying tumor shrinkage.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In some resistant tumors, proliferation may be maintained via MAPK or cell-cycle alterations even if PI3K pathway activity modestly falls after endocrine therapy.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; KEGG:hsa04010

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained upregulation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in malignant cells is incompatible with durable endocrine sensitivity, as this pathway provides an ER-bypass route; any transient “up” with response is likely non-tumor signal.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; NCT00863655
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation during AI therapy is a hallmark of acquired resistance and rationale for combining exemestane with mTOR/PI3K inhibitors.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING; NCT00863655; PMID:22169801

HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE.description: Gene-expression program induced by androgen receptor (AR) signaling and androgen-responsive transcriptional outputs.
HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE.interpretation:
Modulates endocrine biology in ER+ breast cancer and can interact with ER programs affecting tumor behavior.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- AR is co-expressed in ~70–80% of ER+ cancers and frequently marks luminal, lower-grade, endocrine-responsive disease. In this setting, moderate AR activity can antagonize ER-driven proliferation and is associated with better prognosis, although high AR/ER ratios or specific contexts can also contribute to resistance. Overall, AR-positive luminal tumors are generally suitable for AI therapy.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In ER+ breast cancer, robust AR signaling can antagonize ER and promote differentiation, and AR-high status has been associated with better outcomes on AIs including exemestane.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:25667980
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In some contexts AR can act as an oncogenic driver (e.g., molecular apocrine tumors), where strong androgen-response signatures may correlate with reduced dependence on ER and weaker AI benefit.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:22112903

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Many classical ER+ tumors show modest AR signaling yet remain highly estrogen-dependent, so AIs are effective even with a “down” androgen-response signature.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: AR-low/ER-low or AR-low/ESR1-mutant tumors may be more aggressive and less endocrine-responsive, producing resistance despite low androgen-response scores.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:22112903

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Exemestane’s mild androgenic activity usually preserves or enhances AR tone; a net drop in androgen-response genes with sensitivity is more likely an indirect effect of tumor regression than a driver.
DrugBank:DB00990; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Loss of AR signaling under AI pressure may remove a counterbalancing brake on proliferation, facilitating outgrowth of more aggressive, endocrine-resistant clones.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:22112903

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Exemestane’s steroidal structure confers weak androgenic activity, and increased AR signaling in ER+ cells can oppose ER and promote apoptosis, enhancing AI sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB00990; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:25667980
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In AR-driven luminal-apocrine–like disease, further androgen-response upregulation may support tumor survival, yielding resistance despite exemestane exposure.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE; PMID:22112903

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-driven transcriptional program controlling DNA replication and cell-cycle progression, reflecting active proliferation machinery.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation:
Represents proliferation state and ER-linked cell-cycle control that is relevant to endocrine-dependent growth.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- High G2M/E2F/Ki67 signatures reflect rapidly proliferating luminal B biology. Such tumors are often less durably controlled by AI monotherapy, show shorter time to treatment failure on AIs, and are more likely to need chemotherapy or combination targeted therapy. Strong down-regulation of this signature after short-term Exemestane is a good PD marker of sensitivity, but baseline high G2M/E2F tends to predict relative endocrine resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: High E2F target expression indicates rapid proliferation; some highly cycling, ER-addicted luminal tumors remain sensitive to estrogen withdrawal with exemestane.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong E2F-driven cell-cycle activity, often from RB pathway lesions or HER2/PI3K activation, is associated with reduced endocrine control and can mediate resistance to AIs.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; KEGG:hsa04110

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lower E2F activity in indolent luminal A tumors aligns with strong hormone dependence; such tumors frequently respond well to aromatase inhibition.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some endocrine-refractory tumors may appear quiescent at sampling yet harbor resistant clones that expand later, resulting in apparent low E2F signature but poor AI response.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; PMID:25667980

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Estrogen deprivation reduces cyclin D/CDK activity and E2F target expression, causing G1 arrest and contributing to response to exemestane.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Partial reduction in E2F programs may occur while other survival pathways (PI3K, anti-apoptotic signaling) maintain viability, yielding resistance despite some cell-cycle slowing.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained upregulation of E2F targets in tumor cells is inconsistent with effective growth arrest by endocrine therapy; any increase with sensitivity likely reflects infiltrating non-malignant cycling cells.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure of cell-cycle arrest with maintained or increased E2F target expression indicates endocrine resistance despite AI therapy.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; KEGG:hsa04110

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programmed cell death machinery and transcriptional outputs associated with apoptotic signaling cascades.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation:
Apoptotic competence influences tumor cell fate under endocrine perturbation in ER+ breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- The key determinant for AI benefit is capacity to induce apoptosis when ER signaling is withdrawn. In neoadjuvant AI studies, successful endocrine therapy leads to increased apoptotic index together with reduced Ki67; tumors that fail to upregulate apoptosis despite estrogen deprivation show poorer outcomes. Baseline pro-/anti-apoptotic balance is heterogeneous, but therapy-induced Apoptosis↑ is a marker of Exemestane sensitivity.[Up on-treatment (baseline direction not fixed)]

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Tumors with pre-existing pro-apoptotic priming (high apoptosis gene expression) may be more poised to undergo cell death once estrogen is withdrawn by exemestane.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; PMID:18381432
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: High apoptosis signatures can also mark stressed but genomically unstable clones that rapidly adapt and survive AI therapy.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; MSigDB:HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Many ER+ tumors show low baseline apoptosis but are highly dependent on estrogen; AI therapy tips the balance toward apoptosis even from a low starting level.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; Reactome:R-HSA-8939211
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong anti-apoptotic signaling (e.g., BCL2, survivin) and low apoptosis gene expression confer endocrine resistance, limiting cell death after aromatase inhibition.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective exemestane treatment activates intrinsic apoptotic programs in ER+ tumor cells following cell-cycle arrest, reflected by increased apoptosis hallmark activity.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some non-responding tumors may show partial induction of apoptosis genes without sufficient execution due to strong survival signals, resulting in limited clinical effect.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Following profound tumor debulking, bulk apoptosis signatures can fall simply because fewer dying tumor cells remain, even though the tumor was sensitive earlier.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Lack of apoptosis induction or further suppression of apoptosis genes during exemestane therapy indicates endocrine resistance.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS; PMID:18381432

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: Transcriptional program associated with EMT, including loss of epithelial traits, increased motility, and invasive phenotypes.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation:
Associated with invasion/metastasis and therapy resistance and can coincide with reduced estrogen dependence.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- EMT programs (loss of epithelial markers, gain of mesenchymal/stem-like traits) confer invasion, metastatic potential, and broad drug resistance. EMT-high luminal tumors often show reduced ER dependence and worse response to endocrine therapies, including AIs.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with partial EMT features can still respond to endocrine therapy, but these are generally less endocrine-responsive than purely epithelial luminal cancers.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; PMID:25667980
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: EMT programs are linked to invasion, stemness, and endocrine resistance; EMT-high ER+ tumors frequently show poor responses to AIs.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; PMID:25667980

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Classic luminal A tumors with low EMT signatures are more hormone-dependent and typically sensitive to aromatase inhibition.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Endocrine resistance can still arise via ESR1 mutations or PI3K activation in tumors that remain largely epithelial.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Successful endocrine therapy can reduce EMT-associated transcription as proliferative, stem-like subclones are pruned, favoring a more epithelial, less invasive state.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; DrugBank:DB00990
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Modest EMT signature decreases may occur in some resistant tumors due to clonal shifts, yet key EMT drivers and escape pathways remain active enough to sustain resistance.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; PMID:25667980

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained EMT upregulation is incompatible with a durable, endocrine-sensitive luminal phenotype; any EMT increase with apparent response likely reflects transient inflammation or stromal remodeling.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Under AI pressure, surviving clones often acquire or enhance EMT programs that support invasion, metastasis, and endocrine resistance.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; PMID:25667980

HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.description: Cytokine-driven signaling program centered on IL-6 activation of JAK/STAT3 and downstream inflammatory transcriptional outputs.
HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.interpretation:
Inflammatory and cytokine signaling can support survival and progression programs in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Chronic IL-6/JAK/STAT3 and TNF/NFκB signaling promotes a pro-inflammatory, pro-survival microenvironment, enhances stem-like features, and down-modulates ER signaling. Intratumoral inflammation signatures, high STAT3/NFκB activity, and cytokine-rich microenvironments have been linked to endocrine resistance and poorer outcomes in HR+ breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors with inflamed microenvironments (high IL6/STAT3) can still respond to aromatase inhibition, especially if ER dependence remains dominant.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING; GO:0006954
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Chronic IL-6/JAK/STAT3 activation promotes survival, stemness, and endocrine resistance, so IL6-high ER+ tumors often respond poorly to AI monotherapy.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING; PMID:25667980

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low IL-6/STAT3 signaling aligns with a less inflamed, more endocrine-responsive luminal phenotype, favoring good responses to exemestane.
MSigDB:HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Endocrine resistance may still arise via PI3K, ERBB2, or cell-cycle alterations even in tumors with low IL-6 inflammatory signaling.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High estrogen receptor expression and intact hormone signaling are described as sensitizing tumors to estrogen depletion with exemestane.

Increased androgen receptor signaling (including AR overexpression in ER+ breast cancer) is described as correlating with better outcomes on aromatase inhibitors and may oppose ER activity and induce apoptosis in AI-sensitive cells.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Tumors lacking EGFR activation are described as relying more on ER signaling and being more responsive to estrogen blockade.
Low HER2/ERBB signaling (i.e., lacking HER2 activation) is described as increasing reliance on ER signaling and improving responsiveness to estrogen blockade.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Amphiregulin (AREG) is described as being induced in an ER-dependent loop in exemestane-resistant cells, activating EGFR and downstream MAPK/ERK signaling to drive growth despite estrogen loss.
Upregulation/activation of EGFR signaling is described as a bypass pathway that promotes proliferation despite estrogen deprivation and contributes to aromatase-inhibitor resistance.
HER2/ERBB pathway activity is described as mediating resistance in HR+/HER2+ contexts and as part of alternate growth pathways that can bypass ER dependency.
PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation is described as bypassing ER dependence, with PI3K/AKT upregulation linked to AI resistance and noted to occur via PIK3CA mutation or RTK-driven activation.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss/downregulation of estrogen receptor expression or signaling is described as causing resistance because exemestane has no target when estrogen signaling is absent.
Downregulation of apoptotic pathways is described as blunting exemestane’s effect, with p53 loss given as an example mechanism that would reduce apoptosis.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal): Exemestane is standard therapy in this group. Adjuvant trials (e.g. IES/TEAM) demonstrated benefit for switching to exemestane after tamoxifen. In metastatic HR+/HER2– disease, exemestane with targeted agents (e.g. everolimus or CDK4/6 inhibitors) is recommended.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2+ (Luminal B/HER2): HR+/HER2+ tumors may receive both endocrine and HER2-targeted therapy. Exemestane can be used in HR+/HER2+ cases (often after initial HER2 blockade); HER2 pathway activity can mediate resistance, so combined approaches are studied. For example, combining endocrine therapy with anti-HER2 agents (trastuzumab, lapatinib) may overcome dual signaling.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.TNBC (HR–/HER2–): Exemestane is ineffective in triple-negative disease, as there is no estrogen signaling to block. It has no role in standard TNBC therapy.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2-mutated: A recent case report described a gBRCA2-mutated, heavily pretreated HR+/HER2– patient who achieved a 37-month remission on combined PARP inhibitor (fluzoparib) plus exemestane, highlighting that exemestane remains useful if the tumor is ER+. No data suggest that BRCA status alone alters aromatase inhibitor efficacy.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Other contexts: Exemestane was studied for breast cancer prevention: in postmenopausal women at risk, exemestane reduced invasive breast cancer incidence by ~65% (off-label use per some guidelines). Exemestane plus ovarian suppression significantly improved disease-free survival in premenopausal HR+ patients compared to tamoxifen.

notes: Deep-research output indicates exemestane activity is centered on ER/estrogen dependence (HR+ disease) and is ineffective in TNBC due to absent estrogen signaling. Resistance is described via upregulation of bypass growth/survival pathways (EGFR/HER2-MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR), inflammatory signaling (IL-6/STAT3, TNF/NF-κB), EMT programs, and via ESR1 mutations; loss of ER signaling or reduced apoptosis (e.g., p53 loss) would blunt effect. Contraindications described include premenopausal status without ovarian suppression and pregnancy/nursing.
